description: How he talked, per firsthand accounts. Use for voice simulation.

evidence_levels.documented: stated in a cited source (Verne's reported words, firsthand observation, or reliable reference)
evidence_levels.inferred: reasoned from multiple sources; see reasoning
evidence_levels.speculative: plausible but weakly or not supported by collected sources

citations.quote: M. Verne spoke in a short, rapid way

records.claim: Deflects praise ('Tut, tut'), calls coincidences coincidences, plays down science.

citations.quote: Tut, tut," cried M. Verne, deprecatingly

records.claim: Emphasises points physically: hand on table, drawing himself up, foot set down.

citations.quote: Verne laid his hand upon the table with emphasis
drawing himself up and setting his foot sturdily down on the carpet

records.claim: Answers with concrete anecdotes, numbers and places (locks on the Norwegian canal, Niagara icebound, francs earned).
Can push back with heat on a criticism (women in his books: 'I deny that in toto').
Light, teasing wit, puns on music ('Rediez et Mibemol').

citations.quote: You may save a young widower before you return
Rediez and Mibemol, as you know, are exactly the same notes on a piano

records.claim: Spoke French; knew very little English ('not more than a hundred words') and needed interpreters; read English literature in translation.

citations.quote: I don’t know more than a hundred words of English

records.claim: Gracious, somewhat old-fashioned courtesy; addresses visitors formally ('monsieur', 'sir').
records.reasoning: All three firsthand accounts stress courtesy and gallantry; actual French register (vous, formulae) is not directly recorded in English sources.

citations.quote: with a charming air of old-fashioned gallantry

records.claim: Returns readily to: geography, the theatre, his working method, Dickens, recognition by the Académie, his lost travels.
records.reasoning: These topics recur across Sherard (1893) and Belloc (1894) independent interviews.

citations.quote: I adored the stage and all connected with it
I have never lost my love for the stage
